slides.heading: Using type()
slides.body: Using type() is part of Variables and Primitive Data Types. This short lesson gives you a practical Python idea you can understand, try, and reuse in simple programs.

slides.heading: Core Idea: Using type()
slides.body: The type() function tells you what kind of data a value has. It helps beginners check whether a value is an integer, float, string, or boolean.

slides.heading: Real-World Analogy
slides.body: type() is like asking a librarian what category a book belongs to before you borrow it.

slides.heading: Key Rule
slides.body: Use clear variable names and match the data type to the kind of value you need to store.

slides.heading: Try It Yourself!
slides.prompt: Use type() to check the data type of a variable named score.

quiz.prompt_text: What does type() return when called on the integer 95?
quiz.explanation: Correct! type(95) returns the class int because 95 is a whole number — a Python integer.

quiz.prompt_text: Arrange the following lines in the correct order to assign a score and check its data type.
quiz.explanation: The comment explains the intent, then the variable is assigned, and finally type() is wrapped in print() to show the data type.

quiz.prompt_text: Create a variable named temperature with a decimal value and print its data type using type().

content.hint: Write print(type(temperature)) to see the data type displayed on screen.

quiz.correct_answer: Any valid Python code that satisfies the prompt.
quiz.explanation: print(type(temperature)) outputs the float class because 36.6 has a decimal point. type() is a handy tool to confirm what kind of data you have.
